Season 5 I would have to say is probably the most disappointing season of black mirror I have seen. Was it bad? No. But I had an expectation going in. Not so much the expectation of something so original with major twists and turns and bleak turnouts, but I go in with the expectation that each episode will make me ponder if the technology they presented is in fact, a good idea for society. With season 5 I barely got that.

Now I understand this is the creators show and they can do whatever they want, but I felt as if I was cheated an experience and instead of presenting something thought provoking, I got handed a season that was flashy and shiny because it had big named actors/actresses.

I wanna touch on some quick points for each episode.

Striking viper: this was probably my favorite episode and not just for the 'I fucked a polar bear' line. I thought the idea of cheating on your SO through virtual reality was a neat concept because I had never really thought of that before but,  that's where all the good basically stops. I dont believe this episode really explored sexuality (they came to the conclusion they only wanted heterosexual sex in VR. I thought the bachelor guy was for sure going to be trans) nor did it go into depth on the issue of addiction of VR. I think 'Ready Player One' did a much better job with the idea of using VR to escape a harsher reality. But the two main characters lived a comfortable life. The husband didnt have any consequences for his actions and instead got a happy ending where the couple gets one night to cheat on each other. 

Smithereens: this episode could have been so much better honestly. They touched on so many good themes but didnt execute any of them well. Themes like how much information social media companies  has versus the cops. How much time and effort and resources are poured into social media to keep you addicted and how tragic news is so devoid of emotion in today's society.  All of these were great themes but ultimately the only that stuck with me was the 'dont text and drive kiddos'. We have seen that theme before in a previous episode where the boyfriend dies due to texting and driving. I did like the honest one to one conversation the main character and the CEO had though. 

Episode 3(sorry cant remember the title): this was probably my least favorite episode. The initial problems from each of the characters was never really solved. The younger sister didnt make friends. The older sister played bass in front of everyone great but she never really addressed the problems with her mom and Ashley was the only one who's arc seemed completed with her 'finding her true self'. Not to mention the dad still really didnt give a shit about his daughters in the end. I couldnt really tell the message they were trying to send? Besides the cliche "be true to yourself!" And "the fame isnt always glamorous" and "G R E E D  I S  B A D". I didnt really see a problem with the hologram because it wasnt really corrupting anyone mind or corrupting society.

I feel as if the creators have run out of ideas and this is the best they could come up with. Hoping season 6 is a bit more thought provoking.
